chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: The construction industry remains one of the least automated sectors, despite its economic scale and high-risk tasks—especially on roofs. Roof work involves hazardous conditions like falls and repetitive physical labor, making it ideal for robotic automation. Quadruped robots, while increasingly capable, remain underutilized in real-world applications. This work investigates whether commercial quadrupeds like the Unitree Go2 can operate effectively on tiled roofs—a novel, unexplored environment combining steep inclines, smooth surfaces, and discrete structural features.
chk_problem.reason: The poster accurately describes the research problem and motivation, aligning with the reference's focus on the feasibility of quadruped robots for roof environments.

chk_method.label: accurate
chk_method.poster_evidence: A custom test rig simulating a German-style tiled roof (Frankfurther Pfanne) was built to evaluate the Unitree Go2’s performance. Three core locomotion tasks were tested: balancing on increasing inclines, get-up/lie-down sequences in multiple orientations, and incline walking. Motion capture (OptiTrack) tracked foot slippage via reflective markers.
chk_method.reason: The poster provides a clear description of the test rig and evaluation method, matching the reference's details about the experimental approach.

chk_setup.label: accurate
chk_setup.poster_evidence: All trials were automated via Python using WebRTC, with the robot set to standard walking mode at 1.0 m/s. Experiments were repeated 10 times per condition for statistical significance. The setup enabled precise quantification of slippage, trajectory deviation, and critical failure thresholds.
chk_setup.reason: The poster describes the experimental setup, including controlled trials, Python automation, and statistical repetition, consistent with the reference.

chk_primary_result.label: accurate
chk_primary_result.poster_evidence: The Go2 failed to meet manufacturer claims of 40° slope capability. Standing balance failed at 27.58° ± 0.72°, primarily due to front-limb slippage. Get-up/lie-down succeeded only up to 11° (head-up/down) and 7° (sideways), failing when the center of mass exited the support polygon. Incline walking showed a quadratic increase in slippage with incline angle (p < 0.001), with critical failures occurring regularly at 25°. Friction coefficients were 1.144 (flat) and 1.430 (curved).
chk_primary_result.reason: The poster accurately reports the primary results, including the quadratic increase in slippage and critical failures at 25° incline, as well as friction coefficients.
